reasoning:
Key decisions: resend must preserve household_id, template_id, params. R6 says send_sms won't carry those fields; options: build record and call store.append_jsonl directly, or post-extend returned dict — but outbox is append-only, nothing may edit a line after writing. Hmm, "post-extending the returned dict" — the returned dict is the appended record; extending it after append would edit the line? Actually appending to the dict in memory doesn't edit the file. But R6 says "the outbox is append-only and nothing may edit a line after writing" — post-extending the returned dict wouldn't edit the file line, but the file line would lack those fields. Wait — the record appended is the dict; if we extend the dict after append_jsonl, the file already has the short version. So to have full fields in the file, we must build the record ourselves and call store.append_jsonl directly. But then we lose send_sms's ID generation... R2 gives format_sms_id(next_number(...)) — but those are internal functions in notifications/sms.py. The findings name them: format_sms_id, next_number, sent_messages. We could reuse them. But simpler: build record with id via format_sms_id(next_number([m['id'] for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')), phone, text, household_id, template_id, params, queued_at via _now(). Hmm, _now is private. R10 says now() returns 2026-03-10T08:00:00. Actually send_sms uses (now or _now()).

Alternative: call send_sms(phone, text) to get record with id and queued_at, then... we can't edit the line. So better to build the full record and append directly. But then we bypass send_sms's checks — fine, texts are same as original so length ok.

But wait — does the gateway send based on the file? R7: gateway sends every line in outbox. So appending a complete record directly works.

However, using send_sms is preferred ("prefer reusing existing functions"). But send_sms writes incomplete record. R6 explicitly offers "building the record and calling store.append_jsonl directly" as the way to carry household_id etc. So plan: script builds record reusing format_sms_id/next_number/sent_messages from notifications.sms, and _now? Maybe use send_sms's queued_at format: (now or _now()).isoformat(timespec='seconds'). We could import _now. Findings don't name _now explicitly but R10 mentions now(). Hmm, R10: "The operation clock now() returns 2026-03-10T08:00:00 by default". So there's a now() function. Where? Probably in notifications/sms.py or core. Not specified. Safer: call send_sms? No.

Alternative approach: call send_sms(phone, text) which appends record with id/phone/text/queued_at, then... we can't edit. So the record in file lacks household_id. Is that acceptable? Ticket: "re-sends each failed message to the same household, with the same message and details as the original." Details include household_id/template_id/params presumably. R6 flags this as important, implying we should carry them. So build record directly.

For ID: reuse format_sms_id(next_number([m['id'] for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')) as in R2. For queued_at: use _now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')? Findings mention _now in R1 ("queued_at = (now or _now()).isoformat"). So _now exists in notifications/sms.py. We can import it. Or simpler: call send_sms and then... no.

Actually another approach: call send_sms(phone, text) to get the record, then append a second... no, that would double-send.

Hmm, wait — could we call send_sms and then append_jsonl a full record? That would create two lines → two texts. No.

So: script imports from notifications.sms: sent_messages, format_sms_id, next_number, _now (or now). Also store from core.store. Read status via delivery_status() (R4) to get failed ids. Read outbox via store.read_jsonl('outbox/sms.jsonl'). For each failed id, find original record, build new record with same household_id, phone, template_id, params, text; new id; queued_at = _now().isoformat(timespec='seconds'); append via store.append_jsonl('outbox/sms.jsonl', record).

Also update sms_status? New messages have no entry (R4). Not required. Maybe not needed.

Docstring must say it sends SMS (R9). sys.path insert (R9).
